articles.title: New START’s Expiration Will Make the World Less Safe—Even if It Doesn’t Spark Another Nuclear Arms Race
articles.summary: The New START nuclear arms control treaty between the U.S. and Russia has expired. This landmark agreement's lapse introduces significant global uncertainty and raises concerns about a potential new arms race among major powers. The expiration marks the end of the last remaining pact limiting strategic nuclear arsenals, posing challenges to international stability and security.

articles.title: Le dernier garde-fou nucléaire tombe, et les États-Unis et la Russie ont choisi de naviguer à vue (Anglais)
articles.summary: The New START treaty, the last major arms control agreement between the US and Russia, expired on February 5. This critical event removes limits on their strategic nuclear arsenals, potentially initiating a dangerous new arms race. This development significantly challenges global stability, demanding urgent diplomatic efforts to prevent an unchecked military build-up.
